newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks advance to intraday record.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks advance to intraday record.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended earlier gains at mid-afternoon trade on Tuesday as local dealers continued to buy on a change in outlook for the auction of Cetes bills later in the day.
The leading IPC share index was up 52.85 points, or 1.19 percent, at 4,510.82.

"Investors are buoyant, the outlook for the FOMC meeting is favourable. That and the change in market forecasts for this evening's Cetes auction have been driving the market," an equity analyst from the Santander Investment brokerage said.
"We are really surprised by the market's performance," he added.

A Reuters survey of money market dealers showed they forecast bellwether 28-day rates would rise by just 18 basis points at the central bank's primary auction. On Monday afternoon, they had predicted an increase of up to 300 basis points.

"Rationally, one would expect to see profit-taking after the run we've had, but the local interest rate outlook has changed a lot over the last couple of days," said Lars Schonander, head of research at Santander Investment Mexico.
"What this is telling you is there is no evidence of pre-election jitters," he added.

A Reuters survey of nine money market traders taken shortly before the central bank closed bidding, showed they predicted an average rise of 18 basis points on bellwether 28-day Cetes at Tuesday evening's central bank auction.
Dealers said financial stock Bancomer and telecomms firm Telmex drove the market.

Bancomer A series, up 12 centavos to 2.42 pesos, was the most heavily traded stock for the day, closely followed by its B shares, which ended up 9 centavos to 3.91 pesos. The two series together accounted for 21 percent of all shares traded.
"The spread between Bancomer A and B shares is absurdly wide," Schonander said.
Telmex climbed 20 centavos to 19.22 pesos, while its ADRs ended up 5/8 to 48-3/8.
Traders said Telmex ADRs advanced on the back of the Dow Jones, which closed up 49.54 points at 7,722.33 points.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced sliders by 63 to 26 out of a total 116 stocks that traded.
